hero.headline: FBI disrupts threat against Trump UFC event at White House
hero.body:
The FBI has disrupted an alleged threat targeting President Trump's UFC event at the White House, with multiple suspects now in custody, FBI Director Kash Patel announced Tuesday.

Federal officials became aware of a potential threat from individuals outside the Washington, D.C. area on June 10, according to Patel. In a statement, he said that "thanks to the rapid action of this FBI, our partners, and the Department of Justice in a multi-state operation, multiple individuals are now in custody and allegedly planned attacks were stopped cold."

The disrupted plot represents the latest security concern for Trump, who has faced multiple attempts on his life during his presidency. Recent incidents include a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner. Law enforcement agencies across the country are managing what officials describe as an elevated period of political violence.

Patel did not immediately disclose details about the nature of the alleged threat or provide the identities of those taken into custody. He indicated that additional information about the plot would be released once charges are unsealed.

The UFC event took place on the White House south lawn over the weekend, coinciding with Trump's 80th birthday celebration. The event, called UFC Freedom 250, featured a title fight between lightweight champion Ilia Topuria and interim champion Justin Gaethje. The White House had billed it as a historic national celebration, with 4,000 ticketed guests and a fan festival on the Ellipse expected to draw up to 100,000 people.

Sources reported that the alleged threat involved a potential drone attack, though official confirmation of the threat's specific nature remained limited.

The event drew significant attention not only for its security implications but also for statements made by a UFC fighter at the event who made disparaging comments about former first lady Michelle Obama while standing near the president. The incident drew widespread condemnation and raised questions about event protocols.

The FBI's counterterrorism and protective intelligence divisions have intensified monitoring of potential threats against government officials and public events in recent months. Federal law enforcement has increased coordination with state and local agencies to identify and investigate individuals who may pose security risks to high-profile political figures and gatherings.

Meanwhile, UFC president Dana White indicated that another White House fight night may not happen again, citing weather concerns, logistical challenges with constructing the cage and staging events at federal landmarks, and soaring costs that made the event a one-time affair.

The White House has not commented on whether security protocols for future events will be adjusted following the disrupted threat.

cards.headline: Trump announces Iran deal at G7 Summit, urges Israel to reduce Lebanon attacks
cards.teaser: President Trump said at the G7 Summit in France that the Iran deal is complete and predicted the next stage of negotiations will be easier.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a deal to end the war between the U.S. and Iran while attending the G7 Summit in France. He expressed optimism about the agreement and indicated that upcoming negotiations would proceed more smoothly. French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Trump on signing the new Iran agreement.

During the summit, Trump also urged Israel to reduce its military operations against Lebanon. Conservative commentator Bill O'Reilly characterized Israel's response to the Iran deal as significant, noting that Israeli leaders want to maintain the freedom to retaliate against any attacks directed at them.

cards.headline: Iran says U.S. deal requires Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon
cards.body:
Iran has claimed that its agreement with the United States to end fighting includes a requirement for Israeli forces to withdraw from Lebanon. The assertion comes as the two countries work to finalize terms for the ceasefire following weeks of conflict.

Hezbollah confirmed that Iran committed to pursuing the withdrawal of Israeli Defense Forces from Lebanon as part of discussions with Washington. An Iranian official stated to state media that ending the war encompasses terminating what the government characterizes as Israel's occupation of Lebanese territory.

However, U.S. officials have disputed this characterization. They stated on Monday that Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon was not a condition of the U.S.-Iran agreement. American officials emphasized that Israel would retain the right to defend itself against attacks by Hezbollah.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected any immediate pullout, saying his country's forces would remain in Lebanon "for as long as necessary." He told reporters that Israel had established security zones in Gaza, Lebanon, and Syria to protect the nation. "We will remain in these security zones to protect our country," Netanyahu said at a televised press conference.

The agreement has sparked significant backlash within Israel. Netanyahu described the joint U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran as preventing "nuclear annihilation" and said it had pushed away a danger to Israel's population for years. Yet Israeli media outlets characterized the deal as an "abject failure."

The interim agreement between Washington and Tehran explicitly includes a ceasefire in Lebanon, where Israel launched major military operations after Hezbollah attacks on northern Israel triggered the 15-week conflict. Israeli forces currently occupy more than 60 percent of southern Lebanese territory, and sporadic violence has persisted despite the ceasefire announcement.

Hezbollah initially welcomed the U.S.-Iran deal, saying it produced a comprehensive ceasefire including Lebanon. However, the group indicated that its commitment depended on Israel adhering to the agreement's terms.

Israeli opposition figures have criticized Netanyahu's handling of the agreement. Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats party, accused Netanyahu of allowing military accomplishments to be erased. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett said Netanyahu was "incapable of achieving a decisive victory."

Far-right members of Netanyahu's coalition government called for Israel to ignore the deal's terms, arguing that Israel had not participated in negotiations and therefore was not bound by the agreement. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir stated on his Telegram channel that the agreement did not safeguard Israeli security.

An election in Israel is scheduled before October, setting up what analysts expect will be a competitive race for power. Netanyahu announced Monday that he would run and intended to win.

cards.headline: European Union Approves Trade Deal With United States
cards.teaser: The trade agreement negotiated between the EU and President Trump in Scotland moved toward final approval after nearly a year of negotiations.
cards.body:
European Union lawmakers approved a trade deal with the United States that had been under negotiation for nearly a year. The agreement was originally struck between the European Union and President Trump in Turnberry, Scotland, and is now headed for final approval after extended discussions among EU member states.

The deal resolved longstanding trade disputes between the two economic blocs. The approval by EU lawmakers represented a significant step in the ratification process, though the agreement still requires final procedural steps before taking effect.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Begins Meeting Under New Chairman Kevin Warsh
cards.teaser: The Federal Reserve opened its policy meeting with newly appointed Chairman Kevin Warsh facing questions about interest rates, inflation, and central bank independence.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve policymakers convened for their first meeting under Chairman Kevin Warsh, who recently took over leadership of the central bank. Warsh confronts significant challenges including decisions about interest rate policy, managing inflation, and maintaining the Federal Reserve's independence from political pressure.

The meeting marks the beginning of a new era for the central bank as it navigates economic conditions and sets monetary policy. Warsh's approach to these issues will shape the Fed's direction and influence borrowing costs, inflation expectations, and financial markets.

cards.headline: Eight crew members killed in B-52 bomber crash at Edwards Air Force Base
cards.body:
Eight people died when a B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in Southern California during a routine test mission, officials confirmed. The incident occurred at the military installation located in Kern County, approximately 100 miles north of Los Angeles in the Mojave Desert.

Edwards Air Force Base serves as a primary testing site for military and experimental aircraft. The base has historically been the location for numerous aviation milestones and development programs since its establishment. The B-52, a long-range strategic bomber that entered service in the 1950s, was conducting a test flight when the crash happened.

All eight crew members aboard the aircraft were killed in the incident. The base has not yet released the identities of the deceased or specific details about what caused the accident. While the B-52 typically carries a crew of five during standard operational missions, test flights often require additional personnel to conduct specialized monitoring and evaluation activities.

The crash represents one of the deadliest military aviation accidents in recent years. The B-52 fleet continues to serve as a critical component of the United States strategic bomber force. Despite the aircraft's age, the Air Force regularly updates and maintains the planes through ongoing modifications and testing programs designed to extend their operational lifespan.

The Air Force has not announced whether it will ground other B-52 aircraft while investigations proceed. Investigators from the Air Force and other agencies have begun examining the wreckage and flight data to determine the cause of the crash. The investigation process will involve analyzing multiple factors that may have contributed to the accident.

Edwards Air Force Base regularly conducts test flights of both new and existing aircraft as part of ongoing military aviation development and maintenance operations. The remote location and extensive facilities at the base make it well suited for this testing work. The installation has been instrumental in evaluating military aircraft for decades.

The loss of eight crew members represents a significant tragedy for the military aviation community. The incident underscores the inherent risks associated with test flight operations, which often involve pushing aircraft to their limits to evaluate performance and safety systems. Families and colleagues of the deceased crew members are grieving the loss of these service members.

As the investigation continues, more information about the circumstances surrounding the crash is expected to emerge. The Air Force will likely release additional details once investigators have gathered sufficient evidence and completed preliminary analyses of the available data.

cards.headline: Ukraine hits Moscow oil refinery in drone strike
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces struck the Moscow region's largest refinery in retaliation for a Russian attack on a cathedral.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched a drone strike against an oil refinery in the Moscow region during a time when G7 leaders were meeting to discuss increased sanctions on Russian energy. Ukrainian officials identified the target as the largest refinery in the area.

Ukrainian military officials characterized the operation as retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukrainian cultural sites, including damage to churches and monasteries. Ukraine stated it would continue targeting Russian energy infrastructure as part of its military strategy.

cards.headline: European Union approves delayed trade deal with U.S.
cards.teaser: European lawmakers voted to ratify an agreement negotiated with President Trump in Scotland after nearly a year of parliamentary debate.
cards.body:
The European Union Parliament approved a trade deal with the United States that was negotiated with President Trump in Turnberry, Scotland. The agreement now moves toward final approval after nearly a year of legislative debate among European lawmakers.

Members of parliament spent months negotiating the deal's provisions and working toward consensus on its terms before the ratification vote took place.

cards.headline: FBI stops planned attack on White House UFC event
cards.teaser: Multiple suspects are in custody after federal agents disrupted a plot that would have involved a drone strike, according to FBI Director Patel.
cards.body:
The FBI thwarted a plot targeting a UFC event held at the White House, according to FBI Director Kash Patel. Five people were detained in connection with the alleged planned attacks. The event took place over the past weekend.

U.S. media reports indicated the plot would have involved a drone attack. Federal law enforcement disrupted the plan before it could be carried out. Additional details about the charges are expected to be released once they are unsealed.

cards.headline: Hungary blocks Orbán from returning as prime minister
cards.teaser: Hungarian lawmakers voted to limit any prime minister to eight years in office, preventing Viktor Orbán from seeking the position again.
cards.body:
Hungary's parliament has passed legislation imposing an eight-year term limit on the prime minister's office, effectively barring Viktor Orbán from returning to the position. The vote was a key campaign pledge by current Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who promised to prevent his predecessor from seeking power again after taking office.

The measure ensures that no individual can serve more than eight years as prime minister, closing the door on any future political comeback for Orbán.

cards.headline: Russian artist critical of Putin shot dead in Poland
cards.teaser: Robert Kuzovkov, an opposition artist who satirized Vladimir Putin, was killed in Poland while living in exile.
cards.body:
Russian artist Robert Kuzovkov, who also used the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, was shot dead in the eastern Polish town of Biała Podlaska on Monday. He was known for satirical caricatures critical of Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov.

Five shots were fired in the attack, including one to the head, according to a prosecutor in Lublin. Two Belarusians have been detained in connection with the killing, though they have not yet been charged.

cards.headline: Macron and Zelenskyy caught on camera discussing Trump strategy
cards.teaser: French President Emmanuel Macron and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy were overheard planning their approach to President Trump at the G7 summit.
cards.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy were recorded on camera discussing how to handle President Trump during the G7 summit. The conversation occurred as European leaders worked to influence U.S. policy on Ukraine.

Trump signaled a potential shift in focus toward Ukraine as the Iran conflict moves toward resolution. European officials told reporters they have been working to change Trump's position on support for Ukraine, with some progress reported in recent meetings.

cards.headline: FBI arrests multiple suspects in alleged plot to attack White House UFC event
cards.teaser: The FBI arrested several people who discussed plans to attack a UFC event scheduled at the White House, according to FBI Director Kash Patel.
cards.body:
FBI Director Kash Patel announced that the bureau arrested multiple suspects in connection with an alleged plot to attack a UFC event at the White House. According to US media reports, the plan involved a drone attack.

The White House hosted a UFC event called Freedom 250, which UFC boss Dana White indicated would not be repeated. The outdoor event presented logistical challenges, including weather concerns, cage construction, and staging difficulties at a federal landmark, along with substantial costs.

cards.headline: Tropical storm could form in Gulf of Mexico, bringing flood threat to Texas and Louisiana
cards.teaser: A tropical disturbance in the Gulf of Mexico could develop into the first named storm of 2026 and bring heavy rainfall to parts of the South this week.
cards.body:
Weather officials are tracking a tropical disturbance designated Invest 90-L that could strengthen into Tropical Storm Arthur within hours. The system is expected to bring heavy rainfall to Texas and Louisiana, with tropical storm alerts potentially issued soon. Forecasters warn of a multi-day flood threat across the region.

The National Weather Service has issued flood watches for parts of Louisiana extending through the week. Areas including Baton Rouge face elevated flood risks as the system moves through the Gulf. Houston could see heavy rainfall if the system develops as forecast. The disturbance represents the first potential tropical storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season.

cards.headline: Algae bloom turns renovated Washington reflecting pool green after $14.2 million project
cards.teaser: The Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool has turned green with algae shortly after a $14.2 million renovation intended to display an American flag pattern in blue.
cards.body:
The Lincoln Memorial's recently renovated reflecting pool has turned green with algae, undermining the Trump administration's $14.2 million project. The renovation was intended to transform what Trump had called a "filthy" and "dirty" site into a beautiful monument, with the pool's water designed to display an "American flag blue" color.

Despite claims that the renovation would resolve the pool's recurring algae problems, the water has turned green again amid warm weather conditions. The algae bloom has disrupted the planned appearance of the patriotic design that was central to the renovation project's goals.

cards.headline: SpaceX agrees to acquire AI coding company Cursor for $60 billion
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's SpaceX has agreed to buy Cursor, an artificial intelligence startup that automates software coding, just days after the company went public.
cards.body:
SpaceX reached an agreement to purchase Cursor, a company that uses artificial intelligence to automate the process of writing computer code. The acquisition is valued at $60 billion. Cursor recently completed its initial public offering before SpaceX announced the purchase agreement.

The coding startup uses AI technology to help software developers write code more efficiently by automating portions of the development process. The acquisition represents a major expansion for SpaceX into the artificial intelligence sector beyond its core rocket and spacecraft business. The deal combines Musk's space company with a firm focused on AI-powered software development tools.

cards.headline: England replaces injured Livramento with Chalobah for World Cup
cards.teaser: Newcastle United defender Tino Livramento withdrew from England's World Cup squad with a calf injury and will be replaced by Chelsea's Trevoh Chalobah.
cards.body:
England has made a change to its World Cup squad following an injury to Newcastle United full-back Tino Livramento. The defender will miss the tournament due to a calf injury and has been replaced by Chelsea's Trevoh Chalobah.

Chalobah's addition to the squad strengthens England's defensive options as the team moves forward in the competition.

cards.headline: Heavy rainfall forecast for Louisiana parishes as tropical system approaches
cards.teaser: Multiple parishes across Louisiana are preparing for heavy rainfall as Invest 90-L moves through the Gulf of Mexico this week.
cards.body:
Weather forecasters have issued specific rainfall projections for Louisiana parishes as the tropical disturbance moves through the region. The National Weather Service placed Baton Rouge and surrounding areas under a flood watch extending through the week. Heavy storms are expected to continue affecting the region, with elevated flood risks across multiple parishes.

Acadiana and other parts of southern Louisiana face a continued heavy rain threat throughout the week. The Gulf storm system is expected to bring multiple weather impacts as it progresses. Forecasters have provided parish-by-parish rainfall estimates to help residents prepare for the approaching system.

hero.headline: SpaceX Acquires AI Coding Startup Cursor for $60 Billion
hero.body:
SpaceX has agreed to purchase Cursor, an artificial intelligence coding startup, for $60 billion in an all-stock deal announced just days after the rocket company's initial public offering. The transaction marks a significant expansion of SpaceX's operations beyond its traditional aerospace business into artificial intelligence.

Cursor develops technology that uses AI to automate computer code writing. The acquisition represents a strategic move by Elon Musk to advance SpaceX's presence in the competitive AI sector and help the company compete with established players like Anthropic and OpenAI for enterprise customers.

SpaceX had previously negotiated an option to acquire Cursor as part of earlier funding rounds, which the company exercised following its successful IPO. The all-stock structure allowed SpaceX to preserve cash while using its highly valued shares as acquisition currency.

The market responded positively to the announcement. SpaceX shares gained 8% in early trading following the deal's announcement, building on substantial gains from the company's market debut. Shares that initially floated at $135 per share on Friday rose to $207.83 by Tuesday morning, lifting SpaceX's market capitalization to over $2.7 trillion. This valuation temporarily positioned SpaceX ahead of Amazon, which had a market capitalization of approximately $2.65 trillion.

The acquisition represents one of the largest technology deals announced this year and among the biggest purchases of an AI company to date. Industry analysts noted that the transaction reflected both the premium valuations commanded by AI companies and investor enthusiasm for SpaceX's post-IPO prospects.

SpaceX plans to integrate Cursor's AI coding capabilities across its operations. The technology could accelerate software development for rocket systems, satellite networks, and ground support infrastructure. Musk has previously pursued artificial intelligence investments through various ventures, and this acquisition brings substantial AI capabilities directly under SpaceX's corporate structure.

The company indicated in its IPO materials that it sees a $26 trillion addressable market opportunity in artificial intelligence, suggesting the Cursor acquisition aligns with long-term strategic ambitions. The rapid execution of the deal following the public market debut demonstrated SpaceX's aggressive expansion strategy in technology sectors beyond traditional aerospace.

The combined company will leverage Cursor's engineering team and technology platform to strengthen SpaceX's competitive position in enterprise AI applications. By acquiring established AI talent and existing product capabilities, SpaceX avoided the longer timeline associated with building such technology independently.

The all-stock transaction closed quickly, reflecting the confidence SpaceX's leadership and investors placed in the company's newly public valuation and future prospects.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Markets Weigh U.S.-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices continued to decline as traders assessed the implications of the recent diplomatic deal between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices are falling as markets react to a U.S.-Iran agreement. President Trump announced that the deal includes plans to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway in the region. Traders are responding to expectations that reopening this passage could affect oil supply dynamics.

Stock markets showed mixed results following the previous day's strong rallies. The combination of declining oil prices and broader economic uncertainty contributed to uneven performance across major indexes.

cards.headline: Yum Brands Sells Pizza Hut for $2.7 Billion
cards.teaser: Yum Brands agreed to sell its Pizza Hut chain to private equity firm LongRange Capital and Yum China in a $2.7 billion transaction.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Yum Brands completed the sale of Pizza Hut to a consortium consisting of private equity firm LongRange Capital and Yum China for $2.7 billion. The transaction separates the pizza chain from Yum Brands' other restaurant holdings, which include KFC and Taco Bell.

The deal represents a significant restructuring of Yum Brands' portfolio and gives the buyers control of one of the largest pizza chains in the world. LongRange Capital and Yum China will jointly operate Pizza Hut going forward, managing its thousands of locations across multiple countries.

cards.headline: Thames Water Moves Closer to Nationalisation as Government Rejects Rescue Plan
cards.teaser: The British government objected to a proposed rescue deal for Thames Water, moving the troubled utility company closer to public ownership.
cards.body:
Thames Water has moved closer to nationalisation after the government rejected a rescue plan from private sector lenders. The environment secretary determined that the proposed deal failed to adequately protect consumers and the environment.

The rejection significantly narrows Thames Water's options for remaining privately owned as the company faces mounting financial difficulties. The utility serves millions of customers across London and the surrounding regions, making any change to its ownership structure a major development in British infrastructure management.

cards.headline: AI Technology Influences Home Pricing Practices
cards.teaser: Artificial intelligence tools are affecting how homes are priced and sold, according to industry reports examining the technology's role in real estate markets.
cards.body:
Real estate markets are experiencing changes as artificial intelligence technology influences home pricing and sales practices. Reports indicate that AI systems are being deployed to analyze property values, set listing prices, and assist in customer engagement throughout the home buying process.

The technology could reshape traditional agent commission models, according to industry analysis. AI voice systems and predictive algorithms are increasingly being adopted by real estate firms to handle customer interactions and location decisions, marking a shift in how the industry operates.

hero.headline: SpaceX to acquire AI coding tool Cursor for $60 billion in stock
hero.body:
SpaceX has announced a $60 billion acquisition of Cursor, an artificial intelligence-powered coding assistant, in an all-stock transaction completed just days after the company's initial public offering. The deal marks a significant expansion into the software and AI sectors for Elon Musk's aerospace company.

The acquisition comes as SpaceX shares surged following their market debut. On the first day of trading, SpaceX stock jumped 8 percent, lifting the company's market capitalization to approximately $2.7 trillion. This valuation temporarily pushed SpaceX ahead of Amazon, which had a market cap of $2.65 trillion. SpaceX shares are currently trading at $207.83, compared to their initial offering price of $135 per share on Friday.

SpaceX executives pitched the AI opportunity to IPO investors as a major growth area, identifying a $26 trillion addressable market in the sector. The Cursor acquisition represents the company's bet that artificial intelligence capabilities will become essential to its future operations beyond its core rocket launch and Starlink satellite internet services.

Cursor has gained traction among software developers as a tool that uses large language models to assist with code completion, generation, debugging, and understanding. The AI coding assistant competes with similar products offered by established technology companies and other AI firms in the market.

The all-stock structure of the deal allows Cursor shareholders to benefit from any future appreciation in SpaceX's valuation. Since beginning public trading, SpaceX's market value has increased by approximately $1 trillion, driven by investor appetite for the company's space launch capabilities, Starlink operations, and now its AI ambitions.

SpaceX executives have characterized the company's AI division as struggling in the competitive artificial intelligence market. The Cursor acquisition appears designed to help close the gap with established AI rivals such as Anthropic and OpenAI while potentially attracting enterprise customers.

The transaction still requires regulatory approval before closing, which is expected later this year. This acquisition represents SpaceX's most substantial entry into the software domain, marking a strategic shift as the company diversifies beyond its traditional aerospace and telecommunications focus.

The broader market showed mixed results following the SpaceX announcement and IPO performance. The S&P 500 index was up 0.1 percent in early trading, while the technology-focused Nasdaq declined 0.1 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 325 points, or 0.6 percent, to 52,000 points, with gains in financial and technology stocks offsetting losses in other sectors.

cards.headline: ChatGPT market share drops below 50 percent for first time
cards.teaser: The AI assistant remains the most popular worldwide but now faces growing competition from rivals.
cards.body:
ChatGPT's market share among AI assistants has dropped below 50 percent for the first time, signaling a shift in the competitive landscape. The platform remains the global leader with over 1.1 billion monthly users.

Google's Gemini ranks second with 662 million monthly users, while Anthropic's Claude has accumulated 245 million users. The decline reflects increasing competition in the AI assistant space as users explore different tools suited to their specific needs.

cards.headline: India temporarily bans Telegram over exam fraud concerns
cards.teaser: The government ordered restrictions on the messaging app until June 22 and required disabling of message editing.
cards.body:
India has temporarily banned Telegram nationwide until June 22 over concerns that the messaging app facilitates exam fraud. Authorities have also mandated that Telegram disable its message editing feature.

The restrictions stem from Indian officials' assessment that certain platform capabilities have been misused to enable cheating during academic examinations.

cards.headline: Security flaw in Microsoft Copilot allowed theft of authentication codes
cards.teaser: The SearchLeak exploit could have enabled hackers to steal two-factor authentication codes from users.
cards.body:
A critical vulnerability in Microsoft Copilot exposed users to potential theft of two-factor authentication codes. The exploit, called SearchLeak, demonstrated weaknesses in how the AI assistant handles sensitive information.

Security researchers identified the flaw as part of broader concerns about large language model security. The vulnerability highlights recurring issues with how AI systems process and protect user data, raising questions about the industry's approach to securing LLM-based products.

cards.headline: Meta's Threads reaches 500 million monthly users, adds feed customization
cards.teaser: The social platform launched new personalization features including a tool that lets users control their algorithm.
cards.body:
Threads reached 500 million monthly users as Meta introduced new personalization features for the platform. The updates include a tool called "Your Algo" that gives users direct control over their feed content.

These additions reflect Meta's strategy to distinguish Threads from competing social networks and maintain user engagement on the growing platform.

cards.headline: Startup raises $22 million to produce metals without extreme heat
cards.teaser: Foundation Alloy uses mechanical force instead of high temperatures to create alloys for military and consumer applications.
cards.body:
Foundation Alloy secured $22 million in funding to scale production of metals created through mechanical force rather than traditional heating methods. The process involves applying mechanical pressure to shape metals instead of melting them at high temperatures.

The company is developing these alloys for military drones, luxury watches, and chef's knives. Foundation Alloy is expanding its manufacturing capacity as it works to bring this alternative metal production approach to market.

cards.headline: AI startup Probably raises $9 million to reduce hallucinations
cards.teaser: The company aims to prevent factual errors from reaching users and match the accuracy of deterministic systems.
cards.body:
Probably has secured $9 million in funding to develop more reliable AI systems. The startup is tackling one of the industry's biggest problems: preventing language models from generating false information and hallucinations.

The company's goal is to build AI that matches the accuracy and dependability of deterministic systems—traditional software that follows fixed rules and produces consistent results. This focus on trustworthiness addresses a critical need as AI becomes integrated into more sensitive applications.

hero.headline: Serena and Venus Williams receive Wimbledon doubles wildcard
hero.body:
Serena Williams and Venus Williams have been granted a wildcard to compete together in the women's doubles at Wimbledon this month. The All England Club announced the decision on Tuesday morning in what organizers described as one of the most highly anticipated wildcard announcements in recent memory.

The announcement marks a significant moment for Serena, who is returning to professional tennis after four years away from competition. The 44-year-old did not request a singles wildcard and has remained noncommittal about whether she will compete in singles play at the tournament. Venus, who is 46, has also not received a singles wildcard. She has continued to play sporadically on the professional tour since her debut in 1994, taking time away only due to health-related issues.

The Williams sisters are among the most successful doubles partnerships in tennis history. Together, they have won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles, the second-highest total in the Open Era. They have claimed six women's doubles titles at Wimbledon specifically, the highest total in the Open Era at that venue. Their partnership has also yielded three Olympic gold medals in women's doubles, and they reached the number one ranking in WTA doubles.

The wildcard entry allows the sisters to bypass the standard qualification process and compete directly in the main draw. Wimbledon organizers typically reserve wildcard spots for players who may not meet current ranking requirements but have exceptional circumstances or significant historical connections to the tournament. The Williams sisters clearly fit this category given their storied record at the All England Club.

Serena recently returned to competition at Queen's Club, where she won her first match alongside Victoria Mboko against Erin Routliffe and Nichole Melichar Martinez. However, Mboko subsequently withdrew from their next match and the remainder of the grass court season after suffering a torn medial collateral ligament. Serena is continuing her comeback preparations by competing at the Berlin WTA tournament this week alongside world number 10 singles player Karolina Muchova.

The wildcard announcement also included other notable decisions. Maja Chwalinska, who reached the French Open women's singles final as a qualifier, received a wildcard despite not meeting the rankings cutoff. Her sharp recent rise to number 21 in the world rankings will make her an unusual combination of both wildcard and seeded player at the Grand Slam tournament. Additionally, retiring players Stan Wawrinka and Grigor Dimitrov received singles wildcards, while British veteran Dan Evans received a doubles wildcard with compatriot Henry Searle.

The appearance of the Williams sisters will generate significant attention for the tournament and their presence on court together has historically drawn large crowds and television audiences.

cards.headline: Trevoh Chalobah replaces injured Tino Livramento in England World Cup squad
cards.teaser: Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah has been called up to replace Newcastle United full-back Tino Livramento, who withdrew from England's World Cup campaign with a calf injury.
cards.body:
Newcastle United full-back Tino Livramento has been ruled out of England's World Cup campaign due to a calf injury. The setback forces England to make changes to their squad depth.

Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah has been named as Livramento's replacement for the tournament. The swap provides England with defensive cover as they prepare for World Cup competition.

cards.headline: Joe Root captains England on game-by-game basis
cards.teaser: Joe Root says he is taking the England captaincy on a game-by-game basis and admits he has been envious of Ben Stokes for working alongside Brendon McCullum.
cards.body:
Joe Root has stated he is approaching the England captaincy on a "game-by-game basis" rather than planning long-term. The batsman has also admitted to feeling "slightly envious" of Ben Stokes, who has the opportunity to work with coach Brendon McCullum.

Root's comments reflect his perspective on his current leadership role with the England squad.

cards.headline: MLB warns Giants players over Bible verses written on Pride Night caps
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball has issued a warning to San Francisco Giants players who wrote Bible verses on their Pride Night caps, stating they could face consequences for future violations.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball issued a critical statement after San Francisco Giants players wrote Bible verses on their caps during Pride Night. The players denied their actions stemmed from hatred, but MLB determined the writings violated league uniform policies. The incident occurred at a Giants game last week during June's Pride Month celebrations, when the team was acknowledging the LGBTQ community and its baseball fans.

The Giants, based in a city with a large LGBTQ population, typically make significant efforts during their Pride Night game. MLB's response highlighted the tension between players' personal religious expression and the league's strict uniform requirements for special event nights.

cards.headline: Brendan Sorsby enters NFL Supplemental Draft after Texas Tech dispute
cards.teaser: Quarterback Brendan Sorsby plans to enter the NFL Supplemental Draft, ending a legal dispute between Texas Tech and the Big 12 conference over his eligibility.
cards.body:
Brendan Sorsby is entering the NFL Supplemental Draft, ending his time at Texas Tech. The quarterback's decision comes after NCAA betting violations sparked eligibility concerns during the offseason.

The supplemental draft is available to players who missed the standard draft deadline or face college eligibility issues. Sorsby had until June 22 to make his decision. His entry into the supplemental draft resolves the legal disputes that had escalated between the Big 12 and Texas Tech over his playing status.

cards.headline: Derek McInnes expected to move from Hearts to Rangers
cards.teaser: Hearts manager Derek McInnes is reportedly on the verge of switching to Rangers, with his former assistant calling the move a perfect fit.
cards.body:
Derek McInnes is reportedly on the verge of leaving Hearts to become Rangers manager. The move would represent a significant managerial change between two of Scottish football's major clubs.

Tony Docherty, who previously worked as McInnes's assistant, has endorsed the potential move as a "perfect fit" for the manager, suggesting McInnes has the qualities Rangers are seeking in their next leader.

cards.headline: Thomas Tuchel's England extension includes performance clause
cards.teaser: England manager Thomas Tuchel's contract extension contains a performance clause, according to FA chief executive Mark Bullingham.
cards.body:
Thomas Tuchel's contract extension as England manager includes a performance-based clause, according to FA chief executive Mark Bullingham. The clause ties Tuchel's employment to results achieved during his tenure with the national team.

The performance clause represents a shift in how the FA structures agreements with its managerial staff, introducing measurable accountability to the role.

hero.headline: Justice Department Officials Closed Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Review Before Staff Lawyers Could Issue Recommendation
hero.body:
The Trump administration's Justice Department has approved the $111 billion merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, concluding an eight-month antitrust investigation by the department's career staff.

The department announced Friday that it had "completed its analysis of the proposed merger" and determined the transaction would not likely harm competition or consumers across streaming video on demand, linear television, or theatrical film distribution. The approval represents a significant victory for the deal, which combines two major entertainment conglomerates controlling major film studios, cable networks, and streaming services.

The merger combines Paramount's assets including CBS News and Paramount Pictures with Warner Bros. Discovery's holdings of HBO, CNN, and DC Comics properties. Skydance, controlled by the Ellison family, is providing financing for the acquisition. Three Gulf sovereign-wealth funds have committed a combined $24 billion to support the deal.

The Justice Department stated that over the investigation period, it "received from the Parties over two million documents from over 80 custodians, substantial productions of data, as well as extensive documents, data, and advocacy from third parties across the media and entertainment ecosystem."

Paramount responded to the approval by stating the deal is "pro-competitive, resulting in a stronger company better positioned to compete against dominant technology platforms in an industry increasingly defined by intense competition for audiences, talent, technology, and investment."

However, the merger faces continued scrutiny domestically and internationally. The UK's Competition and Markets Authority has opened its own investigation and set an August 7 deadline to determine whether a more in-depth review is necessary. Australian regulators have already approved the deal. More significantly, California Attorney General Rob Bonta indicated Friday that his office's investigation remains ongoing, leaving open the possibility of state attorneys general filing a lawsuit to block the transaction.

Opponents of the merger have criticized the approval. Craig Aaron, co-chief executive of Free Press, stated the "fix was in at the Trump Justice Department from the start," adding that the deal "will undermine competition, destroy jobs, slant the news and endanger our democracy." Senator Elizabeth Warren called the approval "terrible news for every American who doesn't want Trump-aligned billionaires to control what they watch and how much they pay."

The merger also faces internal concerns from journalists. Staff at both CBS News and CNN have expressed worry about potential network consolidation, which could result in significant job cuts. The companies have projected $6 billion in synergies from combining operations. Additionally, some CNN staff have raised concerns about the Ellison family's influence on editorial direction, despite pledges that CNN's editorial independence would be protected.

cards.headline: Grammy Awards Add Five New Categories Including Best Asian Pop Music Performance
cards.teaser: The Recording Academy announced five new award categories and updated eligibility rules for the 2027 ceremony.
cards.body:
The Grammy Awards will introduce five new categories for the 2027 ceremony on February 7. The additions include Best R&B Collaboration, Best Latin Song, and Best Asian Pop Music Performance, marking the Grammys' first dedicated award for Asian pop music.

The Recording Academy also updated eligibility requirements for existing categories, including Best New Artist and Album of the Year. These changes reflect the academy's annual process of soliciting proposals from members to keep the awards aligned with the evolving music industry.

cards.headline: Greta Gerwig's Narnia Film to Get Theatrical Release Through Sony Pictures
cards.teaser: Netflix and Sony Pictures Entertainment agreed to distribute Gerwig's adaptation of The Magician's Nephew in theaters worldwide.
cards.body:
Sony Pictures Entertainment will handle international theatrical distribution for Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew, Netflix announced. The film will be released in IMAX and standard theaters worldwide on Feb. 12, 2027, with sneak previews exclusively in IMAX beginning earlier that month.

The film will debut on Netflix on April 2, 2027, roughly seven weeks after its theatrical premiere. The arrangement represents a collaboration between the streaming service and traditional theatrical distribution, allowing the film to play in cinemas before arriving on the platform. Gerwig's adaptation is based on C.S. Lewis's book from the Chronicles of Narnia series.

cards.headline: John Hannah Confirms Cast Returning for Fourth Mummy Film
cards.teaser: The actor said the new installment will reunite the original cast and be directed by the team behind Ready or Not.
cards.body:
John Hannah confirmed he is returning to the Mummy franchise alongside other cast members from the earlier films. Speaking at the Monte-Carlo Television Festival, Hannah said the fourth installment will bring back the original ensemble. The film will be directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett, who previously directed Ready or Not and entries in the Scream franchise.

Hannah did not specify which other cast members would return or provide details about the film's production timeline. The Mummy franchise began in 1999 with Brendan Fraser in the lead role, followed by two sequels. A 2017 reboot starring Tom Cruise was poorly received and did not continue as a series.

cards.headline: Disney+ Renews Rivals for Third Season
cards.teaser: The streaming service ordered 12 episodes of the period drama ahead of the second half of Season 2 returning in November.
cards.body:
Disney+ has ordered a third season of Rivals, containing 12 episodes. The renewal announcement arrives before the second half of Season 2 debuts in November.

The period drama adapts Jilly Cooper's Rutshire Chronicles novels, which followed residents of a small English village during the 1980s. The series' continuation beyond its initial order reflects strong viewership performance on the streaming platform.

cards.headline: Paddington Musical to Open on Broadway in Spring 2027
cards.teaser: The stage adaptation, which has been running in London, will transfer to New York next year.
cards.body:
Paddington the Musical will open on Broadway in spring 2027 after a successful run in London's West End. The stage adaptation brings the children's book character to the theater, following the popular film franchise that has grossed hundreds of millions of dollars worldwide.

The production joins other family-friendly shows currently running on Broadway. The musical format allows the Paddington character to reach audiences through live theater in addition to films and books. Specific details about the Broadway theater, opening date, and cast were not provided.

cards.headline: CNN Hires Content Creator Kyla Scanlon as Economic Analyst
cards.teaser: The former investment analyst will create explainer content for the network despite having no formal journalism background.
cards.body:
CNN named Kyla Scanlon, a financial content creator and former investment analyst, as a contributor and economic analyst. Scanlon will create explainer videos for the Warner Bros. Discovery-backed network. She does not have formal training in business journalism but has built an audience creating financial content online.

The hire reflects a trend of news organizations bringing in creators who have established audiences on social media platforms. Scanlon previously worked as an investment analyst before building a following by explaining economic concepts. CNN said she will produce content aimed at making economic news more accessible to viewers.

hero.headline: FBI disrupts threat against Trump UFC event at White House
hero.body:
The FBI has disrupted an alleged threat targeting President Trump's UFC event at the White House, with multiple suspects now in custody, FBI Director Kash Patel announced Tuesday.

Federal officials became aware of a potential threat from individuals outside the Washington, D.C. area on June 10, according to Patel. In a statement, he said that "thanks to the rapid action of this FBI, our partners, and the Department of Justice in a multi-state operation, multiple individuals are now in custody and allegedly planned attacks were stopped cold."

The disrupted plot represents the latest security concern for Trump, who has faced multiple attempts on his life during his presidency. Recent incidents include a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner. Law enforcement agencies across the country are managing what officials describe as an elevated period of political violence.

Patel did not immediately disclose details about the nature of the alleged threat or provide the identities of those taken into custody. He indicated that additional information about the plot would be released once charges are unsealed.

The UFC event took place on the White House south lawn over the weekend, coinciding with Trump's 80th birthday celebration. The event, called UFC Freedom 250, featured a title fight between lightweight champion Ilia Topuria and interim champion Justin Gaethje. The White House had billed it as a historic national celebration, with 4,000 ticketed guests and a fan festival on the Ellipse expected to draw up to 100,000 people.

Sources reported that the alleged threat involved a potential drone attack, though official confirmation of the threat's specific nature remained limited.

The event drew significant attention not only for its security implications but also for statements made by a UFC fighter at the event who made disparaging comments about former first lady Michelle Obama while standing near the president. The incident drew widespread condemnation and raised questions about event protocols.

The FBI's counterterrorism and protective intelligence divisions have intensified monitoring of potential threats against government officials and public events in recent months. Federal law enforcement has increased coordination with state and local agencies to identify and investigate individuals who may pose security risks to high-profile political figures and gatherings.

Meanwhile, UFC president Dana White indicated that another White House fight night may not happen again, citing weather concerns, logistical challenges with constructing the cage and staging events at federal landmarks, and soaring costs that made the event a one-time affair.

The White House has not commented on whether security protocols for future events will be adjusted following the disrupted threat.

cards.headline: Newsom demands records from Justice Department investigation
cards.teaser: California Gov. Gavin Newsom's office requested all documents related to a Department of Justice probe into him and his wife.
cards.body:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom's office requested access to all documents and records related to a Department of Justice investigation into him and his wife. In a letter to acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, Newsom's legal affairs secretary David Sapp sought materials including memoranda connected to the probe.

Newsom's office characterized the Justice Department inquiry as a fishing expedition, marking the latest escalation in tensions between the California governor and the Trump administration.

cards.headline: Trump announces Iran deal at G7 Summit, urges Israel to reduce Lebanon attacks
cards.teaser: President Trump said at the G7 Summit in France that the Iran deal is complete and predicted the next stage of negotiations will be easier.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a deal to end the war between the U.S. and Iran while attending the G7 Summit in France. He expressed optimism about the agreement and indicated that upcoming negotiations would proceed more smoothly. French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Trump on signing the new Iran agreement.

During the summit, Trump also urged Israel to reduce its military operations against Lebanon. Conservative commentator Bill O'Reilly characterized Israel's response to the Iran deal as significant, noting that Israeli leaders want to maintain the freedom to retaliate against any attacks directed at them.

cards.headline: Former Social Security administrator calls for raising income cap
cards.teaser: Martin O'Malley said requiring higher-income Americans to pay more into Social Security would solve the program's funding shortfall.
cards.body:
Former Social Security Administration Commissioner Martin O'Malley argued that requiring higher-income Americans to pay more into Social Security is the solution to the program's looming funding shortfall. His comments came after a new report warned that beneficiaries could see a 22 percent cut in their monthly checks in 2032.

O'Malley made the argument in an interview that aired on NewsNation's The Hill program. The proposal addresses funding concerns for the Social Security program as it faces projected deficits in the coming years.

cards.headline: Santa Clara County resident confirmed to have measles after traveling through SFO
cards.teaser: Santa Clara County Public Health warned of measles exposure at San Francisco International Airport and several San Jose locations on June 8.
cards.body:
The County of Santa Clara Public Health Department warned of a public measles exposure in San Francisco International Airport and Santa Clara County. Santa Clara Public Health said the person visited public places while contagious with measles, traveling through SFO and several San Jose locations on June 8.

The infected individual was confirmed as a Bay Area resident. Public health officials issued the warning to alert people who may have been in the same locations during the period when the person was contagious.

cards.headline: Democrats search for next Obama as Ossoff sees growing presidential buzz
cards.teaser: Sen. Jon Ossoff of Georgia is seeing increasing presidential speculation among Democrats as the party searches for its 2028 nominee.
cards.body:
Sen. Jon Ossoff of Georgia is seeing growing presidential buzz among Democrats. The speculation comes as Democrats search for the next Obama and evaluate potential contenders for the party's nomination.

The Hill is hosting a live discussion on whether Ossoff has a chance for the party's nomination. The conversation also addresses the Newsom-Trump feud over the Justice Department investigation and whether the probe might benefit Newsom politically.

cards.headline: AI harm pathways widening faster than misuse detection, report finds
cards.teaser: A new report found that AI capability gains keep widening the number of harm pathways while visibility into misuse grows more slowly.
cards.body:
A new report's most significant shift from the previous year comes through a simple pattern: capability gains keep widening the number of harm pathways, while real-world visibility into misuse grows much more slowly. The findings suggest challenges in controlling AI technology may be accelerating.

The report indicates that the gap between AI capabilities and the ability to monitor their misuse is expanding. This widening disparity raises questions about whether effective oversight mechanisms can keep pace with technological advancement.
